 Pulau Perhentian residents brace for Northeast Monsoon floods 
 By Bernama 
 October 27, 2026 @ 10:18am 
 Residents in the village on Pulau Perhentian here have started making early preparations for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to bring heavy rain and pose a flood risk to low-lying areas of the village. — STR/ZAID SALIM
 JERTIH: Residents on Pulau Perhentian here have started making early preparations for the Northeast Monsoon, which is expected to bring heavy rain and pose a flood risk to low-lying areas. 
 Azizah Ab Rahman, 59, said the area was also vulnerable to flooding, especially when heavy rain coincided with high tides.
 "In the past, the monsoon caused low-lying areas, such as Kampung Tengah, to be flooded up to a depth of almost one metre when rainwater flowing down from the hills could not drain into the sea due to the high tide.
 "As a precaution, I began moving household items to higher ground a few days ago, as floods can occur at any time during the monsoon season," she told Bernama.
 Azizah, who has been living alone since her husband died several years ago, said her children worked and lived on the mainland, leaving her to seek help from neighbours to move heavy items, such as the refrigerator and washing machine, from the kitchen to the higher section of her house.
 She said although the flash floods usually receded within a few hours after the rain stopped, early preparations were important to prevent damage to household items and property losses.
 Another resident, 36-year-old Hayatunnupus Nawawi said she had also placed her refrigerator in the living room on a specially built platform about 1.5 metres high to protect it from floodwaters.
 "I have kept the refrigerator there permanently since last year's incident because it is difficult to move it when flooding occurs.
 "I have two young children, aged five and nine, while my husband, Ali Abdullah, 36, is paralysed," she said.
 Pulau Perhentian Village Development and Security Committee chairman Nik Zawawi Mohd Nor said the floods were generally caused by heavy rain coinciding with high tides during the season, making it difficult for water to drain quickly into the sea.
 "Flooding usually lasts about two hours and may occur several times throughout the MTL season, depending on rainfall and tidal conditions," he added. — BERNAMA
